briefing.text: 'Pathway activation' is a functional claim, shown for example by phospho-ERK or MAPK transcriptional output. Before deciding, list every table and column provided (clinical, gene panel matrix, mutations MAF, SV) and check whether any expression, protein, phospho, pathway-score or functional-assay variable exists. If none does, finding ARAF N217I/G322S only shows that the mutations exist, not that they activate the pathway. Say explicitly which label the available variables can support and why.
briefing.reason: This is the central issue of the task: it decides whether the data can address the claim at all, and it stops activation from being read straight off a mutation list.

briefing.text: Find the ARAF variants by checking Hugo_Symbol==ARAF in data_mutations.txt and ARAF in data_sv.txt. Inspect HGVSp_Short, Protein_position, Transcript_ID, Variant_Classification, genomic Start_Position/codon change and the carrying Tumor_Sample_Barcode. Protein positions depend on the transcript; the canonical ARAF transcript is ENST00000377045 / NM_001654. If the transcript is non-canonical, match on genomic coordinate or codon rather than the 'p.N217I' string. Finding the variants is not evidence for the hypothesis, and not finding them is not evidence against it.
briefing.reason: Exact string matching on the protein change can miss or misidentify the variants. Presence or absence alone is easily misread as support or contradiction.

briefing.text: For the ARAF rows, check dbSNP_RS, FILTER, t_alt_count/t_depth (VAF), and whether the same coordinate recurs across samples. Germline polymorphisms, low-VAF calls and duplicated records should not be counted as somatic activating events.
briefing.reason: Whole-exome MAFs can contain germline or artefact calls that look like recurrent drivers.

briefing.text: Background knowledge, not in the data: ARAF has low intrinsic kinase activity (non-canonical APE motif) and depends on dimerisation, so BRAF-hotspot logic does not carry over. Most ARAF missense variants have no functional characterisation; under AMP/ASCO/CAP and ClinGen/CGC/VICC rules, a novel kinase missense with no functional data is a variant of uncertain significance. Only a few ARAF variants have functional evidence, e.g. the S214 region and beta3-alphaC in-frame deletions. N217 lies near the CR2 S214 regulatory site and G322 near the start of the kinase domain; treat this domain proximity as suggestive only. Check whether any MAF annotation column (SIFT/PolyPhen, oncogenic flags) gives effect calls.
briefing.reason: This prevents a missense in a regulatory or kinase region from being inferred to be activating without a functional or downstream readout.

briefing.text: The cohort is very small, about 8 iCCA samples sequenced by whole-exome. Mutual exclusivity of ARAF with KRAS/NRAS/BRAF/MAP2K1/NF1 mutations or FGFR2 fusions (data_sv.txt) can be tabulated per sample, but only as description. With n<10 it is underpowered and cannot serve as indirect proof of pathway activation.
briefing.reason: This guards against over-reading chance exclusivity patterns as evidence of activation.

shared_assumptions: Both teams read 'the pathway' as the MAPK/RAF-MEK-ERK pathway; the task never names it. Neither team wrote down which pathway or gene set it took the hypothesis to mean, or checked whether another reading would bring other variables into play.

Both teams assumed that only a direct functional readout (expression, phospho-protein, assay) could bear on 'activation', so they treated genomic co-occurrence data as irrelevant to the label. Neither team stated a rule for when indirect genomic evidence counts as 'relevant variables', which is what the task's definition of 'Not verifiable' turns on.

Both teams assumed the two ARAF calls are somatic tumour events. The MAF has no read counts, no matched normal and no Mutation_Status. ARAF is on chrX, and no sex variable exists to interpret allelic state.
unused_evidence: data_sv.txt: every fusion is RNA_support=Yes and DNA_support=No, so RNA-seq was run on these tumours, yet no expression table was provided. Neither team noted this, and it bears on whether a missing readout means a missing variable.
data_sv.txt: RIN1 (a RAS effector) fusions in ICC8, ICC12 and ICC14, including ICC12, which carries ARAF G322S. Both teams tabulated only FGFR2/ARAF SVs as pathway-relevant.

data_clinical_sample.txt TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and the per-sample mutation counts. ICC18 (N217I) has one of the lowest TMBs. Neither team used these to judge whether the ARAF calls could be passenger events.
Hotspot=0 and Annotation_Status in the MAF. Team A reported Hotspot=0; Team B did not use it. Six rows have FAILED annotation (MT/IGR/intron rows, not ARAF).
unresolved_weak_points: Team A named the missing read counts and unverifiable somatic status as its weakest point and only reported it. It did not check whether this affects the label.

Team B's weakest point is a guess about what graders expect, not a property of the data. It gave no data check, and its confidence (0.6) reflects that the label rests on outside expectations rather than analysis.
Neither team wrote out how the three label definitions apply to the variables actually present: ARAF genotype, co-mutations and fusions exist, and an activation readout does not.
second_readings: 'The pathway' could mean MAPK (RAF-MEK-ERK), or more broadly RAS/RTK signalling, which would bring in the FGFR2-PPHLN1 and RIN1 fusions.

'Lead to activation' could be read as a causal/functional claim, which needs a readout, or as a genomic-driver claim (recurrent or mutually exclusive with other MAPK drivers). The second reading could be partly addressed with the variables present, though n=8 limits it.
'ARAF mutations in iCCA' could mean these specific variants as found in this cohort (verifiable presence) or ARAF mutation as a recurrent feature of iCCA (frequency 2/8).
challenge.verdict: Moderately high trust. I confirmed that no expression, phospho or functional variable exists in the five files, so a direct test of 'activation' is impossible. The teams still need to show that their label follows from the task's definitions and not from an untested assumption. They should also account for unused SV evidence (RNA-only fusions, RIN1) and for an ambiguous 'pathway'.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: data_sv.txt shows every fusion as RNA-supported only, so RNA-seq was done on these tumours, but no expression table is in the files. Write down, variable by variable, what the files contain that relates to ARAF and to 'the pathway' (genotype, co-mutations, fusions, TMB), then apply the task's three label definitions to that list. Does that written rule still give your label, and does your reasoning distinguish 'no readout variable' from 'readout unknown'?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your SV check covered only FGFR2 and ARAF. List all fusions per sample, including the RIN1 fusions in ICC8, ICC12 and ICC14 (ICC12 also carries G322S), and record whether any fusion partner is a RAS/MAPK pathway member. Does this change how you define 'the pathway' or your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your stated weakest point is a guess about grader expectations, not a data check. Replace it with a data check: for both ARAF rows, record Hotspot, Annotation_Status, dbSNP_RS, read-count availability, and the carrier's TMB relative to the other 7 samples. Does any of these give evidence for or against the calls being functional or somatic, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: write out which pathway you took 'the pathway' to mean and the exact gene list you searched. Then repeat the search over both data_mutations.txt and data_sv.txt (including the RIN1 and FGFR2 fusions) under a broader RAS/RTK reading. Does a broader reading make any variable relevant to the claim, and does it change your method or label reasoning?

Under standard somatic-variant interpretation guidelines (AMP/ASCO/CAP, ClinGen/CGC/VICC oncogenicity SOP), what evidence is needed to call a non-hotspot kinase missense variant 'activating', and can genomic patterns alone (mutual exclusivity, recurrence) meet it?
questions.why: This decides whether the variables present (genotype and co-mutation patterns) can count as relevant evidence for or against an activation claim, or only a functional readout can.

questions.question: In cBioPortal-style structural-variant files, what does DNA_support=No with RNA_support=Yes mean about the assay used, and does it imply that RNA-seq expression data existed for those samples?
questions.why: Both teams treated the absence of expression data as decisive. Knowing whether a readout was generated but not provided helps frame the 'Not verifiable' reasoning.

findings.question: Under standard somatic-variant interpretation guidelines (AMP/ASCO/CAP, ClinGen/CGC/VICC oncogenicity SOP), what evidence is needed to call a non-hotspot kinase missense variant 'activating', and can genomic patterns alone (mutual exclusivity, recurrence) meet it?
findings.answer: Under the ClinGen/CGC/VICC SOP (Horak et al. 2022), oncogenicity is scored by adding up listed evidence codes. OS2 is well-established in vitro/in vivo functional studies (4 points). OS1 is the same amino acid change as an established oncogenic variant (4). OS3 is a cancerhotspots.org hotspot with at least 50 samples at the position and at least 10 with the same change (4). OM1 is a critical, well-established functional-domain site (2). OM3 is a smaller hotspot (2). OM4 is a different oncogenic missense change at the same residue (2). OP1 is in-silico predictions that all agree (1). OP3 is a hotspot where the same change is seen fewer than 10 times (1). OP4 is absence from gnomAD (1). 'Likely oncogenic' needs at least 6 points and 'oncogenic' at least 10. AMP/ASCO/CAP lists data types but gives no oncogenicity rules; the Horak SOP was written to fill that gap. Mutual exclusivity and co-mutation patterns are not criteria in the SOP. Recurrence counts only at population-hotspot scale (cancerhotspots.org thresholds; COSMIC or a tumour-type-specific study only for tumour types those resources cover poorly), so a handful of cases in one cohort does not qualify. Without functional data, a non-hotspot missense change usually reaches only OM1/OP1/OP4-level points and stays a VUS. OncoKB keeps 'oncogenic' separate from the biological effect (gain-of-function = activating). It gives hotspots based only on statistical recurrence 'Likely Oncogenic', and functional characterisation overrides recurrence. Conclusion: genotype and co-mutation tables alone cannot establish activation, and they cannot refute it either; that needs a functional or pathway readout (e.g., MAPK/ERK phosphorylation, kinase assay, transformation assay).

QUESTION: Under standard somatic-variant interpretation guidelines (AMP/ASCO/CAP, ClinGen/CGC/VICC oncogenicity SOP), what evidence is needed to call a non-hotspot kinase missense variant 'activating', and can genomic patterns alone (mutual exclusivity, recurrence) meet it? ANSWER: Under the ClinGen/CGC/VICC SOP (Horak et al. 2022), oncogenicity is scored by adding up listed evidence codes. OS2 is well-established in vitro/in vivo functional studies (4 points). OS1 is the same amino acid change as an established oncogenic variant (4). OS3 is a cancerhotspots.org hotspot with at least 50 samples at the position and at least 10 with the same change (4). OM1 is a critical, well-established functional-domain site (2). OM3 is a smaller hotspot (2). OM4 is a different oncogenic missense change at the same residue (2). OP1 is in-silico predictions that all agree (1). OP3 is a hotspot where the same change is seen fewer than 10 times (1). OP4 is absence from gnomAD (1). 'Likely oncogenic' needs at least 6 points and 'oncogenic' at least 10. AMP/ASCO/CAP lists data types but gives no oncogenicity rules; the Horak SOP was written to fill that gap. Mutual exclusivity and co-mutation patterns are not criteria in the SOP. Recurrence counts only at population-hotspot scale (cancerhotspots.org thresholds; COSMIC or a tumour-type-specific study only for tumour types those resources cover poorly), so a handful of cases in one cohort does not qualify. Without functional data, a non-hotspot missense change usually reaches only OM1/OP1/OP4-level points and stays a VUS. OncoKB keeps 'oncogenic' separate from the biological effect (gain-of-function = activating). It gives hotspots based only on statistical recurrence 'Likely Oncogenic', and functional characterisation overrides recurrence. Conclusion: genotype and co-mutation tables alone cannot establish activation, and they cannot refute it either; that needs a functional or pathway readout (e.g., MAPK/ERK phosphorylation, kinase assay, transformation assay). HOW SURE: high.
